subject: Redwood Private / VPC vs hyperscalers — follow-up & next tests
messages:
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sun, 15 Mar 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Demo recap — Private/VPC requirements and hyperscaler comparison

Hi Alice — thanks again for the time today. Quick recap / proposed next steps so we stay aligned: 

Summary of what I heard: 
- Primary requirement: private VPC deployment (no public egress) or an air-gapped on-prem option for PHI workloads.
- Secondary: KMS/HSM integration for key material, audit logs & retention, and predictable latency for 95th percentile calls (sub-150ms target for our 512 token payloads).
- Procurement timeline: target decision by end of Q2; initial PoC in Apr.

How Redwood compares to the hyperscalers (short):
- Hyperscalers (AWS/Google/Azure): managed endpoints but control plane and some telemetry typically traverse public networks; less flexibility for fully air-gapped installs and harder to guarantee zero-egress configurations.
- Redwood Private: can run a private control plane in your VPC or entirely self-hosted on-prem (air-gapped package). No mandatory outbound egress when deployed in your network. We support KMS/HSM integrations (AWS KMS / CloudHSM, Azure KeyVault HSM options) and provide audit log exports to your S3/Blob store or central SIEM.

Proposed immediate next tests for the PoC: 
1) Network & install checklist: we provide a short firewall checklist and an architecture diagram (attached) to confirm network requirements.
2) Private control plane deploy in a non-prod VPC + smoke test (verify no egress, KMS handshake).
3) Latency comparison: run the same inference workload against your existing hyperscaler endpoint and Redwood Private in-VPC to compare 95th percentile latency and token cost.

Attachments: redwood-private-arch-diagram.pdf, redwood-enterprise-security-pack.zip (SOC2 / controls summary).

Can you confirm: (a) who from your infra/procurement should we loop in for network & license questions, and (b) any blackout dates in Apr for a PoC kickoff?

Thanks — I’ll follow up with a PoC runbook we can use to scope the effort.
— Vanessa

Subject: Re: RE: Demo recap — Private/VPC requirements and hyperscaler comparison

Hi Alice — quick tech reply to the three questions: 

1) Control plane location: We offer three options — (A) Redwood-managed hosted control plane (default) which communicates over TLS to the compute plane; (B) Private control plane deployed into your VPC (control plane VMs and management endpoints live in your account; Redwood has no access unless explicitly configured by you); (C) On-prem / air-gapped deployment where both control and compute are installed inside your network with no outbound connectivity. For PHI use-cases you can choose B or C and we’ll provide deployment artifacts & runbook.

2) Firewall checklist: For option B (control plane in your VPC) there are no mandatory outbound public IPs — the control plane lives in your VPC and talks to compute nodes over internal networking. If you choose option A (hosted) we list a small set of egress endpoints (HTTPS to telemetry endpoints) — but for this PoC we recommend option B. I’ve attached a short PoC runbook (poc-runbook.md) and the architecture diagram Vanessa attached. The minimal ports for the PoC (option B) are TCP 443 for admin API & TLS and SSH 22 only if you want interactive support (otherwise we use SSM/session proxies).

3) HSM/KMS: We support AWS KMS + CloudHSM for key protectors (you can configure a customer-managed KMS key and we never store plaintext keys). For an air-gapped on-prem install we integrate with local HSMs via PKCS#11-compatible drivers.

Proposed PoC scope (high level): 
- Week 0: network sign-off & schedule
- Week 1: deploy private control plane in a non-prod VPC + install Redwood compute nodes
- Week 2: run latency/cost comparison and basic throughput tests + verify KMS handshakes

We’ll pull together a short quote for the two options (dedicated reserved vs on-prem license) and share it by EOD Wednesday.

Marissa
